# Welcome!

* In this demo we will see how to use OpenCV to track an object in a video. We'll first select the object (Region Of Interest) then track it through the frame and finally we' ll plot the evolution of the barycenter of the object with regard to the frame number.

* The notebooks can be executed online with binder [![Binder](https://mybinder.org/badge_logo.svg)](https://mybinder.org/v2/gh/AlexandreDabySeesaram/Tracking_video/main?urlpath=lab/tree/./demos/) (no download required).

To run the notebook locally you'll need to setup an environment with opencv, matplotlib and numpy. Follow these steps to create a Conda environment named `tracking-ev` with Python 3.13 and all required packages:


```bash
# Create a new conda environment with Python 3.13
conda create -n tracking-env python=3.13 -y

# Activate the environment
conda activate tracking-env

# Install required packages: OpenCV (with contrib modules), NumPy, and Matplotlib
conda install -c conda-forge opencv=4.8.0 matplotlib numpy -y
```
